sections.h2: What should a Matthews homeowner weigh before selling?
sections.html:
Matthews is a high-value, high-income town, and the 2027 Mecklenburg County revaluation will reset every assessment in it. The Census Bureau estimates 32,769 residents for July 2025, compared with 29,435 in 2020 and 27,198 in 2010, across 17.12 square miles of land.

That mix of rising values and a pending county reappraisal gives sellers a timing question. Some will prefer to close before new assessments arrive in early 2027, while others will wait for them. Whether you list with an agent, sell on your own or accept a cash purchase of the house in its present condition, find out how the new county values could look to a buyer.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Matthews homes?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts lists a midpoint owned-home value of $445,100 for 2020 to 2024, higher than the figures for nearby towns such as Kannapolis or Kernersville. The table lists the main housing and income numbers.

Owner costs have a midpoint of $1,986 a month with a mortgage and $591 without. Residents 65 and older account for 20.5%, foreign-born residents for 13.4%, and 15.4% of people speak another language at home. Poverty is 3.7%. Retail sales in 2022 reached $1,657,448 thousand, and health care and social assistance receipts were $542,603 thousand, which shows a town whose economy reaches well past its own housing.

sections.h2: How will the 2027 revaluation affect a Matthews sale?
sections.html:
Mecklenburg County values every parcel again as of January 1, 2027, and Matthews property is covered. The county revalues every four years, a schedule it began in 2019, so this is a regular cycle with no one-time surprise.

The county's November 2, 2026 update says 428,506 residential and commercial parcels have gone through an initial review. After that review, the median increase is about 15% for residential property and about 30% for commercial property, and staff continue reviewing through the rest of 2026. New values are scheduled to be announced and notices mailed in early 2027. The county presented an update to the Matthews Board of Commissioners on September 28.

  • The Board of County Commissioners approved the 2027 Uniform Schedules of Values, Standards and Rules on October 6.
  • Owners can check their property record card at Reval.MeckNC.gov and report errors, such as a wrong bathroom count.
  • Tax rates are set by city, county and town elected officials in the spring, and the bill is mailed in summer.

The county says rates are adjusted after a revaluation to keep revenue neutral unless elected officials choose otherwise. Until rates are adopted, treat any estimate of a future tax bill as a guess.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Mecklenburg County value in Matthews?
sections.html:
Ask for an informal review within 30 days of the date on your notice, or take a formal appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review. The county's revaluation page gives both options, and its Office of Tax Administration accepts appeals online.

State law shapes what follows. The equalization board's first meeting falls between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May, and a hearing request has to be made before it adjourns. If the board mails its decision, you have 30 days from that mailing to file a written notice of appeal with the Property Tax Commission, and a copy goes to the county assessor. The assessed value is not your sale price, but a lower value can reduce your cost of owning the house until closing.

sections.h2: What is Matthews like for buyers?
sections.html:
The town's website points to several features that buyers notice. Matthews is home to the Mecklenburg County Sportsplex, the Matthews Heritage Museum, Matthews Playhouse, a public library and a visitor center, and it runs community events such as Summerfest, Beats 'n Bites, Alive and Winter Wonderlights.

  • The Silver Line light rail, a Silver Line Task Force and Matthews transportation projects such as John Street and the Northeast Parkway appear on the town's site.
  • Greenways include the Four Mile Creek Greenway and the Matthews Heritage Trail through historic Crestdale.
  • The town's departments cover police, fire and EMS, public works with stormwater and street maintenance, planning, and code enforcement.

The website also lists a bond referendum titled Moving Matthews Forward, with parks and transportation bonds, and a proposed one-cent sales tax for transit and roads. Because these are proposals, ask the town for their current status before relying on them in a listing.

sections.h2: What closing steps does a Matthews seller face?
sections.html:
The deed is filed at the register of deeds for the county where the land lies. North Carolina law makes the seller pay an excise tax of one dollar per $500 of value, and the office collects it before recording. Unpaid property tax is a lien on the parcel, so any balance is cleared at closing.

Recording order protects buyers, since a conveyance counts against lien creditors only from the time it is registered. If tax goes unpaid for years, the county can foreclose the lien in an action similar to a mortgage foreclosure, with a public sale at the courthouse door and redemption available before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs. A payoff letter and a title search before you list help avoid surprises.

sections.h2: Which route fits a Matthews seller?
sections.html:
Each route trades price, time and effort differently.

  • An agent listing can capture strong demand for well-kept homes and takes weeks for showings and negotiations.
  • A private sale saves a commission and requires you to manage buyers and paperwork.
  • A cash purchase accepts the house as it is and can close on your schedule, usually at a discount.

If you are weighing timing around the revaluation, compare offers in writing and ask what each buyer assumes about taxes.

faqs.q: When does Mecklenburg County's next revaluation take place?
faqs.a: The county values all property as of January 1, 2027. New values and notices are scheduled for early 2027, and the county revalues every four years.

faqs.q: How much have Mecklenburg values risen in the initial review?
faqs.a: The county reports a median residential increase of about 15% and a median commercial increase of about 30% after the initial review. Final assessed values will be posted in 2027.

faqs.q: How long do I have to ask for an informal review?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date on your notice, according to the county's revaluation page. A formal appeal goes to the Board of Equalization and Review.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in a Matthews sale?
faqs.a: The seller. North Carolina charges $1.00 for each $500 of value, and the register of deeds collects it before recording.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Matthews?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists $445,100 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. Your house may differ, so use nearby sales and the county record card.
